```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>",
  eval = requireNamespace("tma",  quietly = TRUE) &&
         requireNamespace("rENA", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

This article walks through fitting a standard **ENA** (undirected) model and
an **ONA** (directed) model from the built-in `RS.data` dataset, then
rendering both as live interactive plots with `qeviz`.

## Data and model setup

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(qeviz)
library(tma)
library(rENA)

data(RS.data)
```

```{r model-spec}
units_by <- c("Condition", "UserName")
codes    <- c(
  "Data", "Technical.Constraints", "Performance.Parameters",
  "Client.and.Consultant.Requests", "Design.Reasoning", "Collaboration"
)

hoo_rules <- tma::conversation_rules(
  (Condition %in% UNIT$Condition) & (GroupName %in% UNIT$GroupName)
)
```

```{r accumulate, message=FALSE}
context_model <- tma::contexts(
  RS.data,
  units_by  = make.names(units_by),
  hoo_rules = hoo_rules
)

multidim_arr <- tma::context_tensor(
  RS.data,
  sender_cols    = NULL,
  receiver_cols  = NULL,
  default_window = 8,
  default_weight = 1
)

result_ena <- tma::accumulate(
  tensor        = multidim_arr,
  codes         = codes,
  context_model = context_model,
  ordered       = FALSE
)

result_ona <- tma::accumulate(
  tensor        = multidim_arr,
  codes         = codes,
  context_model = context_model,
  ordered       = TRUE
)

ena_set <- rENA::model(result_ena)
ona_set <- rENA::model(result_ona, directed = TRUE)
```

## Creating a plot object

`qe_plot()` wraps a set object in a `qe_plot` that can be passed through the
chain API.  No rendering happens yet — the plot is fully lazy.

```{r plot-objects}
qe_ena <- qe_plot(ena_set)
qe_ona <- qe_plot(ona_set)
```

Inspect what groups and units are available:

```{r introspect}
qe_groups(qe_ena)
head(qe_units(qe_ena))
```

## Standard ENA (undirected)

Show both group mean networks overlaid.  Each chain call returns a new
`qe_plot` — the original is unchanged.

```{r ena-overlay, results='asis', echo=TRUE}
p <- qe_ena |>
  qe_group() |>                                  # show all group means + CI
  qe_edges(qe_groups(qe_ena)[1],
           also = qe_groups(qe_ena)[2])          # overlay both networks

htmltools::HTML(qe_fragment(p))
```

Compare groups by subtraction — positive weights favour the first group,
negative weights favour the second:

```{r ena-subtraction, results='asis', echo=TRUE}
p_sub <- qe_ena |>
  qe_group() |>
  qe_edges(qe_groups(qe_ena)[1],
           compare = qe_groups(qe_ena)[2])

htmltools::HTML(qe_fragment(p_sub))
```

## ONA (directed)

Directed edges are rendered as tapered arrows whose apex points toward the
stronger directional contributor.

```{r ona-plot, results='asis', echo=TRUE}
p_ona <- qe_ona |>
  qe_group() |>
  qe_edges(qe_groups(qe_ona)[1], also = qe_groups(qe_ona)[2])

htmltools::HTML(qe_fragment(p_ona))
```

## Individual unit networks

Use `qe_units()` to list unit IDs, then pass one to `qe_edges(unit = ...)`.
The group mean markers stay visible so the individual network can be read
in context.

```{r unit-network, results='asis', echo=TRUE}
unit_id <- qe_units(qe_ena)[1]
cat("Plotting unit:", unit_id, "\n")

p_unit <- qe_ena |>
  qe_group() |>             # show all group means for context
  qe_edges(unit = unit_id)  # individual edge network

htmltools::HTML(qe_fragment(p_unit))
```

## Adding unit points

`qe_points()` overlays the individual unit scatter dots:

```{r with-points, results='asis', echo=TRUE}
p_pts <- qe_ena |>
  qe_group() |>
  qe_edges(qe_groups(qe_ena)[1]) |>
  qe_points()

htmltools::HTML(qe_fragment(p_pts))
```

## Label control

`qe_labels()` controls label visibility for nodes, group means, and unit
points independently.  Accepted values: `"on"`, `"off"`, `"click"`,
`"auto"`.

```{r labels, results='asis', echo=TRUE}
p_labels <- qe_ena |>
  qe_group() |>
  qe_edges(qe_groups(qe_ena)[1]) |>
  qe_points() |>
  qe_labels(nodes = "auto", means = "on", points = "click")

htmltools::HTML(qe_fragment(p_labels))
```

## Exporting standalone files

`qe_export_html()` writes a self-contained HTML file — no server or
internet connection required:

```{r export, eval=FALSE}
qe_export_html(qe_ena |> qe_group() |> qe_edges(qe_groups(qe_ena)[1]),
               "ena_plot.html")

qe_export_html(qe_ona |> qe_group() |> qe_edges(qe_groups(qe_ona)[1]),
               "ona_plot.html")
```

Branching from a common base works naturally since each chain call copies
the plot:

```{r branching, eval=FALSE}
base <- qe_ena |> qe_group()

qe_export_html(qe_edges(base, qe_groups(qe_ena)[1]), "group1.html")
qe_export_html(qe_edges(base, qe_groups(qe_ena)[2]), "group2.html")
qe_export_html(qe_edges(base, unit = qe_units(qe_ena)[1]), "unit1.html")
```
